Resolved conflict: ethylene is not what switches mango to flowering. Cool weather (subtropics) or shoot age with low gibberellin (tropics) does that. In Florida, ethylene stayed at basal levels in buds and leaves, and ethephon raised it without causing flowering; in the Philippines, blocking ethylene did not stop KNO3 from working. Rises reported in India and the Philippines go along with developing flower buds, so they are a consequence, not a cause. Ethylene may still help buds that are already floral to break evenly.
